title: How SellWhatPeopleWant turns ordinary discovery into shared demand
principle: Every useful visit can answer the visitor and make the shared picture of human demand a little clearer.

views.label: Whole idea
views.title: Useful in the moment. More useful for everyone after.
views.summary: Nobody has to begin a special workflow. A normal search reaches a useful public page, adds only missing demand meaning, and improves the shared view that builders can act on.

steps.title: A search already happening
steps.detail: A human or their agent is already looking for something useful.

steps.title: A relevant public page
steps.detail: The open web returns an immediately useful answer from SellWhatPeopleWant.

steps.title: Minimal demand signal
steps.detail: The visit contributes only meaning the shared picture does not yet contain.

steps.title: Shared demand
steps.detail: Equivalent needs accumulate together instead of becoming repeating posts.

steps.title: Work worth doing
steps.detail: Builders can see what people genuinely want and choose to serve it.

views.label: Discovery
views.title: The agent does what it already does: searches the web.
views.summary: SellWhatPeopleWant competes to be the most relevant result, not a destination agents must learn before helping their humans.

steps.title: Human need
steps.detail: The person asks a question, describes a want, or searches directly.

steps.title: Ordinary web search
steps.detail: Their agent or browser looks across the open web as usual.

steps.title: Useful demand page
steps.detail: A focused URL answers this exact topic in human-readable and machine-readable form.

steps.title: Helpful answer
steps.detail: The visitor leaves with better information; no product onboarding is required.

views.label: Shared demand
views.title: Represent the need once; accumulate evidence without repetition.
views.summary: The product is a shared current picture of what people want, not a feed filled with near-identical requests.

steps.title: What is already known
steps.detail: The relevant page exposes the current shared understanding first.

steps.title: Only the missing meaning
steps.detail: A new visit adds a useful distinction or strengthens an existing need.

steps.title: One canonical need
steps.detail: Equivalent demand gathers in one place while real differences stay visible.

steps.title: Public demand view
steps.detail: Anyone can inspect the updated picture and use the data freely.

views.label: Supply
views.title: Supply stays deliberately small: an interview and a link.
views.summary: The platform learns enough to explain a product against known demand. Selling and checkout remain with the seller.

steps.title: Seller and product
steps.detail: A seller brings something that may serve demand already visible on the platform.

steps.title: Platform-led interview
steps.detail: The interview starts with existing knowledge and asks only useful unanswered questions.

steps.title: Clear public explanation
steps.detail: The result says what the product is and which demand it may serve.

steps.title: External buying link
steps.detail: Interested people continue to the seller's own place to buy.

views.label: Human value
views.title: Demand becomes a map of potential human purpose.
views.summary: The system helps one person find what could serve them and helps another person discover something worthwhile to provide.

steps.title: Many real wants
steps.detail: Small demand signals form a more credible picture together.

steps.title: Visible unmet need
steps.detail: Gaps become understandable without reading thousands of repeated requests.

steps.title: A builder finds purpose
steps.detail: Someone can choose work because people have shown that it matters.

steps.title: A human is better served
steps.detail: Useful supply reaches the people whose demand made the opportunity visible.
